The *Minelapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha Ap 204) is a short verse text located within the Therāpadāna collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. As with other compositions in the collection, it recounts the past meritorious deeds and karmic fruit of an elder (thera) centered on a devotional offering of flowers (*minela* blossoms) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records five modern translations in five languages [SuttaCentral].

No direct external parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan are identified by SuttaCentral or DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. In addition, the text shares standard formulaic verse sequences with numerous other flower-offering accounts in the *Therāpadāna*, such as the *Punnāgapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 335 and Tha-Ap 161), the *Aggapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 262), and the *Sālapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 235) [DharmaNexus].
